items.title: Apply now for the Trellis 30 Under 30 climate leaders 2026
items.summary: The annual Trellis 30 Under 30 list honors individuals who have made a specific, direct, measurable impact by addressing climate change through their professional roles.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark turns away from ‘natural’ trees to make toilet paper
items.summary: Two years after making a “natural forest-free” paper sourcing commitment, Kimberly-Clark is building a manufacturing plant to scale its use of hesperaloe, one of 70 regenerative natural fibers it has tabbed as an alternative to wood pulp.

items.title: UK’s over-reliance on climate-vulnerable countries threatens fresh food supply
items.summary: The UK imports 40% of its food, a significant portion from countries now battling escalating climate risks.

items.title: New guide aims to help councils unlock community solar
items.summary: With Great British Energy set to open a new Partnership Fund for joint council and community energy projects soon, a new guide aims to help these collaborations scale.

items.title: edie 27 launches Energy Zone to connect solution providers with businesses investing in efficiency, security and decarbonisation
items.summary: As organisations face rising costs, energy security concerns, regulatory pressure and the need to decarbonise, decision–makers are looking for practical ways to reduce consumption, improve performance, strengthen resilience and prove the return on investment from energy upgrades.

items.summary: Join us on 17 September for a unique opportunity to gain expert-led insights through thought leadership and industry panels featuring top professionals in sustainability, supply chain and procurement.

items.title: Q&A: What is ‘long-duration energy storage’ – and why does the UK need it?
items.summary: The UK is pioneering the use of “ super batteries ” that can store energy for long periods, smoothing the output from wind and solar power as the country moves towards net-zero.
